strategy_roster.name: JBrainTrend1Stop
strategy_roster.notes: Jurik MA is approximated by EMA(7) and the Stochastic by RSI(9), keeping the documented 47/53 neutral bands and the ATR(7)/2.3 swing trigger; the extended ATR(10)*1.5 stop line, SignalBar delay and automatic reversal are not DSL features.

strategy_roster.name: ColorXvaMA Digit StDev
strategy_roster.notes: Deviation bands are EMA(20) plus/minus K2=2 and K1=1 standard deviations of STD(20); the docs list only parameter names, so these lengths and multipliers are stated defaults. The short branch is dropped because the engine is long-only and no stops are documented.

strategy_roster.name: Early Open Trend
strategy_roster.notes: The wick-based confirmation around the session open becomes a bar that sweeps its open and closes back on the bullish side, with the mirrored sweep as exit. The 07-18 session window, 20:00 flatten, once-per-day gating, DST offsets and 100/1000-pip protections are time features and price units, so SL/TP stay null.

strategy_roster.name: SVOS EURJPY D1
strategy_roster.notes: VHF is unavailable so the trending/ranging regime uses ADX(20); the trending branch uses the documented MACD(10,25,5) histogram cross and the ranging branch an RSI(8) recross, with a bearish-bar/engulfing proxy as exit. Pip-based 350/90/150 stops, the 0.3 std-dev floor, doji divisor and order caps are dropped.

strategy_roster.name: Liquidex V1
strategy_roster.notes: WMA is approximated by SMA(20) (MaPeriod has no documented value) and the buy rule is an open below the average with a close above it; the opposite cross reverses per the docs. RangeFilter and StopLoss are absolute price/point units that do not translate.

strategy_roster.name: Fibonacci Retracement Strategy for Crypto
strategy_roster.notes: The 61.8% entry and 23.6% long-exit retracements are computed from the 20-bar Donchian high/low; the docs give no lookback value so 20 is a stated default. The 38.2%/78.6% short legs are omitted for the long-only engine.

strategy_roster.name: Simple Fibonacci Retracement
strategy_roster.notes: Uses the documented LookbackPeriod = 100 and the long branch of the level cross at 61.8% (the docs leave the chosen level open). The 50/20-pip take-profit and stop are price units, not percentages, so the loss of the level supplies the exit instead.

strategy_roster.name: Gold Friday Anomaly
strategy_roster.notes: This is a purely calendar-driven EA: it buys the first Friday candle inside a date range and exits after a fixed 4-bar hold, with no market-derived condition. The DSL has no weekday/date field, so the never-true guard is used rather than inventing a signal.

strategy_roster.name: Spearman Rank Correlation Coefficient
strategy_roster.notes: The signal is a rank correlation between two separate securities (threshold 0.8 over 10 bars) traded as a pair, which a single-symbol backtest cannot observe. The never-true guard is used to avoid fabricating a long leg.

strategy_roster.name: Close Orders Risk Control
strategy_roster.notes: A risk-management overlay that liquidates existing orders when floating P&L hits the target or cut-loss, with no entry logic and no percentage thresholds. The never-true guard prevents inventing a market signal.
